description:
Hi, I’m Maanav Krishna—a second-year developer specializing in AI/ML, Python, and data-driven backend engineering, with experience shipping prototypes across global hackathons (NVIDIA, PayPal, and Amazon).
I’m tackling Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data, working with NASA’s microgravity combustion datasets to surface actionable fire-safety insights for future space missions.
summary:
HALO is an interactive, SI-powered dashboard that turns NASA’s microgravity fire data into fire-safety answers for Moon habitats.

The problem: NASA’s recommended Moon-habitat air is about 34% oxygen at 8.2 psia, but no solid-fuel test in NASA’s PSI combustion archive that records its oxygen goes above 22.2%, and none of the 33 tests in the challenge’s Moon window burned a real cabin material.

HALO summarizes, ranks and interprets all 24 PSI combustion investigations (1,225 test rows) for any habitat you enter. It grades how well tested evidence covers your air (Artemis Base: D), ranks the investigations that matter most, shows what your smoke detector would likely miss (15 of 35 Kapton fires caught; 35 of 35 with ionization), and names the one new test that would close the biggest gap (30% O2 at 10 psia).

Every number is computed by code and cited to NASA data; the SI explains, never invents. HALO shows where the evidence ends, before the first fire on the Moon does.
details:
What it does HALO answers one question for anyone designing a lunar habitat: would NASA's fire tests cover my habitat's air? Enter an atmosphere (O2 and pressure), airflow, cabin materials and smoke detectors, or pick a preset (ISS, Moon Envelope, Artemis Base, Pressurized Rover, EVA Suit). HALO returns a cited Fire Brief:

  • Evidence grade (A–F). How close tested evidence comes to your air, using an evidence distance stated on the Method page, d = √((ΔO2/10)² + (Δp/3)²) with rings at 0.5, 1 and 2. Results on NASA's data: ISS B, Moon Envelope C, Rover C, Artemis Base D, EVA Suit F. A grade describes evidence coverage, not safety.
  • What would raise this grade. The same engine shows that Artemis Base would go from D to B if NASA's Saffire IV–VI flight reports were archived in PSI, and to C after one new test. Both are marked hypothetical.
  • Detector blind spot. In NASA's SAME and SAME-R flight data, an ISS-style scatter detector stayed below its alarm level in 20 of 35 Kapton smoke runs. Adding an ionization channel catches 35 of 35. All of that smoke data comes from ISS air, and HALO says so.
  • The next test to fly. HALO searches candidate conditions for the single new test that most reduces the evidence gap: a real cabin solid at 30% O2, 10 psia, taking Artemis Base from 2.47 to 0.72.
  • Coverage map. The whole O2 × pressure plane, shaded by grade, with every NASA test point, the Moon window and the presets. Drag "your habitat" across it and watch the evidence run out.
  • Ask HALO. Ask a question about your brief and get a plain-words answer that cites its facts.
  • Also included: Explore and compare all 24 investigations, a material screener, partial-gravity bounds, print-ready briefs and a CSV export of every cited test row for modelers.

Key findings from NASA's data

  1. No solid-fuel PSI test row that records its O2 is above 22.2% (142 eligible solid rows, 13.6–22.2%). Inside the Moon window (≥30% O2, ≤10.2 psia), 0 of 33 rows is a real cabin solid: 20 are gas flames and 13 are a surrogate burner.
  2. Smoke-detector blind spot for overheated plastics (above).
  3. In FLEX droplet burns, flames went out on their own more often with CO2 or helium than with nitrogen as the inert gas: at the six O2 levels all three gases share, 84% and 90% vs 66%. Fuel mix and pressure differ, so HALO reports this as an association, not a measured suppression effect.
  4. The cheapest gap-closer may be archiving data NASA already has: the Saffire IV–VI results exist only as reports, not in PSI.

Why you can trust the numbers (Validity)

  • Every number on screen is a "fact" with a provenance badge (measured, assumed, inferred, literature, computed, model, SI) and a source link (PSI DOI or NTRS report).
  • We re-checked HALO's data against NASA's live PSI repository. All 24 combustion datasets are covered, the raw files are byte-identical to what NASA serves, and all 1,225 rows were recomputed with zero mismatches.
  • CI rebuilds the app's data from NASA's raw files on every change, and 577 automated tests run: 84 pipeline, 377 engine and app, 116 end-to-end.
  • Known judgement calls, such as the 2.0 V detector proxy and the distance scaling, are stated on the site's Method page.

Impact NASA's exploration atmosphere studies point to oxygen-enriched, low-pressure air for Moon habitats, and the Artemis program is moving towards Moon habitats. HALO helps habitat and equipment designers choose atmospheres, materials and detectors with eyes open, and gives test planners a concrete, computed case for the next experiment. On Earth, the same smoke-detector gap matters wherever plastics overheat; the brief ties its findings to four NASA Spinoff fire technologies.

How it is creative Instead of another data dashboard, HALO grades the evidence itself: where NASA's tests stop, what they can and cannot vouch for, and the single experiment that would extend them. The coverage map, the "what would raise this grade" ladder and an assistant that can only restate checked facts are new ways to make an archive actionable.

Tools

  • Python 3.14 data pipeline (pandas, scikit-learn) building a versioned JSON data contract.
  • TypeScript engine with Next.js 16, React 19 and Tailwind 4, hosted on Vercel.
  • zod validation. Vitest and Playwright tests.
  • GitHub Actions CI with CodeQL.
  • Code: https://github.com/MaanavKrishna/HALO (Apache-2.0).

Use of SI (disclosed)

  • The numbers. All grades, distances, counts and model outputs are computed by code, never by SI.
  • Ask HALO and summaries. An LLM writes plain-word explanations (Ask HALO) and the short summaries of the 24 investigations. Every SI sentence is marked with an "SI" chip on the site. A validator rejects any answer with a number that is not a cited fact, and the site then shows code-written text instead.
  • Code and video. An LLM coding assistant helped write code, and all data processing, models and copy were reviewed by the author. The demo video was edited with SI assistance around real screen captures of the live app.
  • The ideas and the method are the my own.
